bibliography.abstract: This study examines the socio-economic determinants of per capita household carbon dioxide (CO₂) emissions in Lucknow, India, using primary data collected through personal interviews with 270 households. Per capita CO₂ emissions from electricity consumption, LPG use for cooking, and private vehicle use were estimated using the emission coefficient method (ECM). The effects of socio-economic and demographic factors on emissions were analysed using ordinary least squares (OLS) regression with a double-log specification. The results show that per capita household income is the strongest predictor of electricity- and transport-related emissions. A 1% increase in per capita household income is associated with a 0.50% increase in per capita electricity emissions and a 1.07% increase in per capita transport emissions, while its effect on LPG emissions is not statistically significant. Households located in developed urban areas are associated with higher electricity- and transport-related emissions, whereas households belonging to relatively advantaged socio-economic groups exhibit higher electricity-related emissions. Household size and age exert varying effects across emission sources, highlighting the importance of household composition in shaping energy use. The findings underscore the role of socio-economic and spatial inequalities in determining urban carbon emissions. By incorporating India-specific socio-cultural factors such as caste and intra-urban disparities, the study contributes to the growing literature on household carbon emissions. Although the findings are associational and primarily applicable to rapidly urbanizing tier-2 Indian cities, they highlight the need for targeted climate policies promoting sustainable consumption, energy-efficient technologies, improved public transport, electric mobility, and climate-sensitive urban planning.
bibliography.title: Socioeconomic determinants of per capita household carbon dioxide emissions: evidence from Lucknow India

en.caveats: The findings are purely associational and may only generalize to similar rapidly urbanizing tier-2 cities in India.
en.what: This study estimated per capita household carbon dioxide emissions from electricity, LPG cooking, and private vehicles for 270 households in Lucknow, India, using the emission coefficient method and double-log OLS regression. A 1% increase in per capita household income was associated with a 0.50% increase in electricity emissions and a 1.07% increase in transport emissions, while LPG emissions showed no significant change. Higher emissions were also linked to households in developed urban areas and those from advantaged socio-economic and caste groups.
en.why: It provides empirical evidence on how intra-urban spatial disparities and India-specific socio-cultural factors, such as caste, shape household carbon footprints in a rapidly urbanizing tier-2 Indian city.
